_comment: The tactical migration set's outward calls into SHARED, non-exclusive code -- the half of
the effect surface the inventory is structurally blind to (docs/dead-ends.md G59).
MEASURED, then classified per body. Opened by TACT-CUT 2026-08-25; consumed by TACT-CUT2,
which will move the ones that need a gate into `select.effect_names` + the domain's
effect_classes file. NOT yet gated -- this file is the finding, not the fix.
WHY THE INVENTORY COULD NOT SEE THESE. Effect membership is a name prefix or a named wall,
and a wall is a member of the tactical closure by construction. This domain declares no
prefixes on purpose (no prefix predicate survives its closure -- docs/dead-ends.md G47), so
both halves of the predicate only ever match code INSIDE the closure. Everything a member
calls out into shared territory -- the resource loader, the input queue, the UI blit
primitives, the strategic roster, the PRNG -- fell through in silence while the report read
31 of 31 classified, 31 of 31 verified, zero unclassified, zero stale.
THE CLASS IS THE TWICE-TEST: is running this body twice, back to back, with the same
inputs, observationally different from running it once? `twice_test` records the answer and
the accumulator (or its absence) that decides it -- not whether the body reaches a device
API, which is the rule that cleared a read-modify-write framebuffer brighten (G58).
`entry_owned` IS THE REASON THIS IS NOT A LIST EDIT. A gate is a hook over the first eight
bytes, and SEVEN of these entries already have an owner: the harness pins llm_rand and
time_GetCurrentTime with whole-body install_jmp replacements, seams/video.cpp holds
llm_gfx_apply_window_resolution (the D13 re-entrancy guard) and llm_view_set_size_mode (the
D13b picker), save/save_live.cpp holds map_LoadPlanetFromDisk, and the sim promotions hold
llm_strat_unit_remove_from_map / llm_strat_unit_teardown. Two owners of one entry is C4.
mh::effects::defer_entry() is the existing answer -- but each needs its own argument for why
the owning mechanism already fires the effect once, and llm_rand's is the awkward one: the
pin replaces the body with an LCG that STILL ADVANCES, so a double draw is still a double
draw.
Produced by .claude/workflows/tact-cut-shared.js -- classify then adversarially verify with
the default set to disagree. All 31 reviewed, ZERO overturned. One evidence correction is
recorded inline on llm_strat_unit_teardown.

GetResourseFilePtr.why: The resource-load entry point: rsr_GetFileEntry(fileName) locates the pack entry, then the body does CALL file_seek (0x004cf0a9, repositions the pack's shared file handle), CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf0b4, fresh heap allocation), CALL utils_read_from_file (0x004cf0e1, real disk I/O into that buffer), and on an 'LZW' magic match a second CALL utils_malloc (0x004cf110) + CALL LZW_Decompress (0x004cf12a) + CALL utils_free (0x004cf135) of the first buffer.
GetResourseFilePtr.evidence_addr: 0x004cf0a9 (CALL file_seek -- first irreversible action) and 0x004cf0e1 (CALL utils_read_from_file -- the actual disk read)
GetResourseFilePtr.twice_test: YES, differs. Two back-to-back calls perform two file seeks + two disk reads and hand back two DISTINCT freshly-malloc'd buffers (plus, on the LZW path, a second decompress + a second free of a different allocation) -- exactly the doctrine's 'a file opened or written' / 'a handle allocated' / 'memory freed' trigger list, not a restorable pure computation.

Two back-to-back calls do two seeks, two reads, and hand back two distinct pointers -- textbook doctrine trigger (handle/allocation, disk I/O). Own body does the I/O directly; none of its callees (rsr_GetFileEntry, file_seek, utils_malloc/free, utils_read_from_file, LZW_Decompress) are in the 56-target gate list. No existing hook.

llm_fatal_cleanup.twice_test: YES, catastrophically. This is a one-shot process-fatal teardown: CoUninitialize a second time on an already-uninitialized COM apartment, freeing already-freed graphics/font/sound resources, releasing already-released DirectDraw surfaces, and re-deleting already-deleted save temp files are all real double-free/double-teardown hazards -- the doctrine's own framing ('un-play a sound... un-write a file') applies directly to llm_game_clear_save_temp_files and to the DirectSound/DirectDraw teardown calls.

llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.why: In-place RGB565->RGB555 squeeze over the caller's sprite_blob pixel array: for every pixel it reads *local_24 (MOVSX at 0x0043c84e), computes ((v&0xffc0)>>1)+(v&0x1f), and writes the result back into the SAME slot (0x0043c873) before advancing the pointer. The write target is also the read source of the transform, so the transform is applied to its own prior output on a repeat call.
llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.evidence_addr: 0x0043c873 (MOV word ptr [EDX],AX -- the accumulating store back into the pixel just read at 0x0043c84e)
llm_gfx_convert_pixels_565_to_555.twice_test: YES, differs. First call converts real RGB565 data to RGB555 once. A back-to-back second call on the same buffer treats the already-squeezed RGB555 bits as if they were still RGB565 and reapplies the same shift/mask, producing garbage pixel values different from a single conversion -- structurally identical to the doctrine's brighten-RMW example, just for this format instead of the framebuffer.

llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.why: Own body sets position/color globals then unconditionally calls llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped (0x004a2d08 -> 0x004a2fdc), which I decompiled fully: for each covered glyph pixel it reads the CURRENT destination pixel byte (`(char)*psVar14` at 0x004a30ba, used as a LUT index alongside the source coverage/color) and writes the LUT-blended result back into that same destination pixel (0x004a30de). That is a genuine alpha-blend read-modify-write against the framebuffer, not a plain overwrite.
llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.evidence_addr: 0x004a30b0/0x004a30ba (MOVZX reads of the existing dest pixel byte) and 0x004a30de (MOV word ptr [EDI],BX -- write of the blended value back into that same dest pixel), inside llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped
llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb.twice_test: The accumulator is the destination pixel itself: blend(dst) = LUT_A[f(dst_lo)] + LUT_B[f(dst_hi,color)], then dst := blend(dst). Running the glyph draw twice back-to-back re-reads the ALREADY-BLENDED pixel as the new 'dst' input on pass two, producing a different (typically further-blended/darker) color than a single pass -- observably different from running it once. Classic non-idempotent alpha-blend RMW, same shape as the doctrine's dashed-outline phase-rotate example.

time_GetCurrentTime.why: Reads _G_LLM_GAME_CLOCK_RAW_TICKS (0x00e654e4, the deterministic SIM clock, not OS wall time despite the CRT-style name), FILDs it, FDIVs by a constant (DAT_0x00500204), FSTPs/FLDs the double result, and returns. No writes anywhere in the body.
time_GetCurrentTime.twice_test: NO -- pure read of the sim-clock global that this function's own body never advances; two back-to-back calls (with no intervening tick) return identical values. Independently confirmed by the project's own docs: src/mh_dll/mh/addr/mh_effects.gen.h:535 explicitly notes "time_GetCurrentTime (also reached) is a pure clock read, not itself part of the effect chain" for an unrelated gate target that reaches it, and src/mh_dll/libmh/lockstep/timekeeper.cpp:104 calls it as a plain `mh::call::time_GetCurrentTime` (an ordinary call-table entry, not a gate/replace).
time_GetCurrentTime.entry_owned: YES -- src/mh_dll/mh_harness/harness.cpp P0-SPDET: `[harness] pin_wallclock=1` (default 0) does install_jmp(ADDR_GET_CUR_TIME, pinned_get_current_time), a WHOLE-BODY replacement. Found by the verify stage, not the classify stage.

review.reason: Verified full .asm: reads _G_LLM_GAME_CLOCK_RAW_TICKS, FILD/FDIV/FSTP into a stack-local, returns it. No global writes anywhere in the body -- correctly pure as a standalone function. (Separately, this function's ENTRY has a conditional whole-body replacement elsewhere in the tree -- see global_findings; that does not change the behavioral classification of the original body, only the entry-ownership picture.)

utils_str_cmp.why: Word-at-a-time string comparison using the classic 0xfefefeff/0x80808080 zero-byte-detection trick, reading through param_1 (EBX) and param_2 (EDX) only. Every instruction in both exit paths (LAB_004d1744: SUB EAX,EAX; LAB_004d176a: SBB EAX,EAX / OR AL,0x1) operates on registers only -- no memory store anywhere in the 0xa1-byte body.
utils_str_cmp.twice_test: NO -- pure comparison of two byte strings in memory it never modifies; calling it twice on the same two pointers returns the same result both times.
utils_str_cmp.entry_owned: none found -- only the generated MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_utils_str_cmp macro exists; not invoked under mh/seams or mh/hook. No mh_effects.gen.h gate target.

review.reason: Verified full .asm: classic word-at-a-time zero-detection string compare, both exit paths operate on registers only, no store to memory anywhere in the body.

w_sprintf.why: Formats varargs through the shared formatter __uprtf (CALL 0x004e08d7 at 0x004d033b) into the caller-supplied `dst` buffer, then NUL-terminates it (MOV word ptr [EDX],0x0 at 0x004d0346). Every write lands in the caller's own output buffer, computed purely from the read-only format string + varargs -- e.g. the game's own text-scratch buffer (G_TEXT_TMP) per numerous src/mh_dll/libmh/sim/*.h comments describing it as writing 'only the non-hashed text-scratch buffer'.
w_sprintf.twice_test: NO -- given the same dst/format/args, both the formatted characters and the NUL terminator are unconditional overwrites of the same buffer bytes; a 2nd call reproduces byte-identical buffer content. No global/persistent state beyond the passed-in destination buffer is touched.
w_sprintf.entry_owned: none found, and structurally CANNOT be owned via the standard export-gate path: src/mh_dll/mh/addr/mh_export.gen.h defines `MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_w_sprintf(IMPL) static_assert(false, "w_sprintf: MH_UNAVAILABLE__varargs_cannot_be_marshalled")` -- the varargs shape blocks the normal replace/shadow marshalling mechanism outright. It is called only via raw function-pointer casts (libmh/lockstep/rx_dispatch.cpp, turn_engine.cpp, timekeeper.cpp) at its real address, never hooked.

review.reason: Verified w_sprintf's own .asm: calls the CRT formatter __uprtf (a known Watcom printf engine per notes/2026-07-19.md) which writes into the caller-supplied dst, then NUL-terminates dst[written]. Did not fully trace __uprtf's own internals (not exported locally, large CRT routine) so I cannot 100% rule out an internal locale/rounding-state global, but this is a standard library formatter and the claim (writes only the caller's buffer, deterministic given same format+args) is consistent with how it is used and documented elsewhere in the tree. Slightly lower confidence than the fully-traced item

llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16.why: ADDED 2026-08-28 (TACT1E debt drain, session 2026-08-28-0127) -- a SECOND instance of G59's blind spot found while arming llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw: this callee is not one of the original 31 tact-cut-shared.js edges, but reaches the SAME hazard llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb already documents in this file. get-decompilation on llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped (0x004a2fdc, reached via llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16 -> llm_gfx_draw_text_blend_clipped, 0x004a2c8e -> the glyph-blend body) confirms: per covered pixel it reads the CURRENT destination short via `(char)*psVar14` (line 74 of the decompile) as a LUT index and writes the blended result back to that same `*psVar14` (line 81) -- a genuine self-referential alpha-blend RMW against the UI surface pixels, identical shape to llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb's entry below. find-cross-references confirms 7 distinct tact-domain callers reach it directly (not through llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb, which is llm_tact_frame's own separate wrapper).
llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16.twice_test: YES, fails -- identical reasoning to llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb's entry: blend(dst) = LUT_A[f(dst_lo)] + LUT_B[f(dst_hi,color)], dst := blend(dst). A second back-to-back call re-reads the ALREADY-BLENDED pixel as input, producing a different result than one call.
llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16.entry_owned: none found -- only the generic MH_EXPORT_REPLACE_llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16(IMPL) macro definition exists in mh_export.gen.h; no gate entry, no seams/hook reference.
llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16.note: NOT YET GATED (same posture as the rest of this file -- the finding, not the fix). llm_tact_ui_char_panel_row_draw's dll_shadow_manifest.json entry was reverted to arm_ready:false after this was found (it had been armed on the strength of the closure tool's 22 declared regions, none of which cover the actual blended pixel target -- a computed pointer, invisible to the region sweep the same way view_shift's writes are). The other 6 callers listed above should be checked before arming any of them for the rig too.

review.reason: Independently re-derived from the raw decompilation of llm_gfx_font_draw_glyph_blend_clipped rather than assumed from the sibling llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb entry: confirmed the same *psVar14 read-then-write pattern at lines 74/81 of the get-decompilation output, and confirmed via find-cross-references that llm_ui_text_draw_rgb16 is a genuinely separate call edge from 7 tact members, not a re-listing of the already-documented llm_gfx_draw_text_rgb path (which only llm_tact_frame calls).
